transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-04-23
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samir Kaur (Redwood CSM); Maya Thompson (Stratus Security), Eric Liu (Platform), Dana Park (CTO)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan from Redwood here, our SE Priya and Samir from customer success are on. How are we doing?
[00:10] Maya (Stratus): Hi Jordan, thanks — doing good. We've been evaluating a few inference providers and security is the gating factor for us. So wanted to run through posture, compliance and what a pilot would look like.
[00:22] Jordan: Great — that's exactly what we want to cover. Quick agenda: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML + SCIM, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency and network options — hosted vs dedicated vs private. Sound good?
[00:35] Dana (CTO): Yep, that covers it. Our compliance team needs SOC2 Type II and ideally ISO 27001. Also we need the ability to force SSO and central provisioning.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): Totally get it. At a high level, for Hosted we have a SOC2 Type II report and customers can use SSO/SAML + SCIM; Dedicated gives isolated capacity and more control over retention windows; Private lets you run in your VPC or on-prem with full network controls and KMS integration.
[01:05] Eric (Platform): Can you elaborate on the KMS/HSM story? We need to ensure keys are customer-managed and that tokenization keys never leave our control.
[01:15] Priya: For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with support for customer-managed keys via cloud KMS providers — AWS KMS, Google KMS, Azure Key Vault. For Private deployments we can integrate with your HSM or bring-your-own-KMS; keys never persist in Redwood's control plane in those setups. There's a nuance with Dedicated where we offer customer KMS integration as well, but we need the keystore to be accessible from the capacity — we can walk through the exact network setup in the deep dive.
[01:40] Maya: Are there exportable logs for forensic investigations? Our auditors want immutable audit trails.
[01:50] Priya: Yes. We have an audit log stream. For Hosted customers we retain audit logs for a default window (configurable) and can push logs to customer-owned sinks — S3, GCS buckets, or syslog — depending on the model. For Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and direct export to your SIEM. Logs include request metadata, auth events, model version, and responses metadata, though payload redaction is supported.
[02:15] Jordan: Quick note — some transcription in my notes might say "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, but that's just me writing quickly.
[02:22] (laughter)
[02:28] Dana: Important for us: data residency. We have EU customers and need data at rest to live in the EU and for audit artifacts to be in region. How does Redwood handle that?
[02:40] Priya: We support region pinning on Hosted for supported models and can enforce region routing. For Dedicated you can provision capacity in the desired region. For Private, obviously you control the region. We'll need to confirm region availability for the specific model variants you plan to use — some smaller model builds might not be in every region.
[03:05] Maya: What about retention and deletion? The legal team wants a straightforward retention policy and ability to purge historical inputs on request.
[03:15] Priya: We have configurable retention for request/response logs and KV caches. For Hosted we can set default retention and support on-demand deletions; for Dedicated/Private customers have direct control. We can provide deletion SLA language in the contract.
[03:30] Eric: Any limitations on token-level data retention for caching? We don't want accidental persistence of PII in the KV cache.
[03:38] Priya: You can disable prefix/KV caching per route or per model. We also offer automatic redaction and prompt-scoped caching controls. For the pilot, we typically recommend disabling caching for PII-heavy routes and enabling selective caching for performance-critical stateless calls.
[03:58] Maya: On authentication — SSO enforcement and role mapping. We use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. Can we enforce SSO for all org users and map groups to RBAC roles?
[04:10] Jordan: Yes. Redwood supports SAML-based SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync. RBAC supports role-to-group mappings, admin roles, and API key scoping. Priya, can you mention the admin audit features?
[04:22] Priya: Sure — admin actions (role changes, token creation, route updates) are logged in the audit trail with user + IP + timestamp. We also have change history in the Console for critical configs. For higher assurance we can provide read-only audit exports and connect to your SIEM via streaming.
[04:40] Dana: Good. For Dedicated/Private, how isolated is the control plane? We want our team to manage keys and networking, but not expose anything to other tenants.
[04:52] Priya: Dedicated capacity runs in isolated pools bound to your account — customers don't share GPUs. The control plane is multi-tenant for Hosted but we provide strict access controls and encryption. Private deployment gives you a private control plane option so you manage access and networking fully. We'll show the architecture diagram in the follow-up where you can see where the control plane sits and how the data path works.
[05:15] Eric: Firewall rules — what do we need to open for Private? Any inbound from Redwood? We prefer inbound blocked and allow outbound only.
[05:25] Jordan: Private deployments can be configured to require outbound connections to Redwood for management, or made fully air-gapped if you want on-prem. For VPC peering we provide a list of CIDR ranges and ports; typical required egress is to the control plane endpoints for metrics and updates. We'll share the network template.
[05:45] Maya: On compliance docs, will you provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA?
[05:50] Jordan: Yes — we can share the SOC2 report and ISO summary under an NDA. I'll attach them to the follow-up email.
[05:58] Priya: Also we'll include a short doc on our encryption-at-rest approach, key lifecycle, and an FAQ on KMS integration pitfalls we've seen during pilots.
[06:10] Dana: One more — penetration testing and vulnerability disclosure. Do you run regular pentests and have a program?
[06:18] Priya: Yes — we run annual or continuous pentests and maintain a vulnerability disclosure program. We can share a summary of our last pentest scope and remediation timeline.
[06:28] Maya: For the pilot, our security team may want at least one dedicated security sync with your SE to go over any nitty-gritty network and KMS stuff.
[06:36] Jordan: Totally — we recommend a SE-led deep dive with your platform/security engineers. Priya, available next week for a deeper session?
[06:42] Priya: Yes, I have slots Wed/Thu. We can book a 60-minute session to walk network diagrams, KMS flow, and a hands-on run-through of audit exports.
[06:54] Eric: On the pricing side, if we go Dedicated vs Hosted, what are the contract implications? We want to know lead time for capacity and minimums.
[07:04] Jordan: Dedicated is capacity-reserved and usually requires a short provisioning lead time depending on region; there are commit levels for monthly throughput. Hosted is self-serve; Private is quote-based and often requires an engagement for install and ops. We'll include a short pricing/commitment summary in the follow-up.
[07:22] Dana: Any known compatibility issues with our environment? We run Kubernetes on AWS, standard VPCs, and we use Okta for SSO.
[07:32] Priya: Okta + SAML + SCIM is a common pattern. For KMS integration, AWS KMS in your account is supported. On Kubernetes, if you do Private on EKS we provide Helm charts and an operator for installation.
[07:45] Maya: A few small clarifications: 1) we need proof that logs are tamper-evident; 2) we need to define retention buckets per dataset; 3) we want the ability to mass-revoke API tokens.
[07:58] Priya: Logs are checksumed and we can stream to your immutable storage for tamper-evidence. Retention buckets per dataset is something we can model in the pilot config. Mass-revoke tokens is supported via admin console + API; we can also programmatically revoke tokens if you need automation.
[08:20] Jordan: Great — to recap next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO under NDA, network template, RBAC/audit papers, and propose times for a SE-led technical deep dive. Customer to provide traffic profile for pilot sizing.
[08:35] Dana: That sounds right. We'll review and get Eric's traffic numbers over to you.
[08:42] Jordan: Awesome — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invites.
[08:48] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional overlap and filler words removed for readability; some product names may be slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache).
questions: Can Redwood provide SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 artifacts under NDA?
Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM for Hosted/Dedicated/Private?
Can audit logs be exported to customer SIEM and configured for immutable retention?
What firewall/networking rules are required for Private/VPC peering?
Is SCIM supported for user provisioning and group-to-role mapping?
